scenes.title: What you're borrowing
scenes.narration: You're borrowing £256,500 to buy a home worth £285,000. That's 90 percent of its value. Lenders call this your loan to value. You'll pay it back over 30 years.

scenes.title: Why your loan to value matters

visual.heading: Borrowing more than 85% of the value
visual.body: Rates are usually higher at this level. Your loan to value falls as you repay.

scenes.narration: Loans above 85 percent of a home's value usually have higher rates. Each payment you make lowers your loan to value. When your fixed rate ends, you may have more deals to choose from.

scenes.title: Your fixed rate
scenes.narration: For the first 2 years, your rate is fixed at 4.89 percent. Your monthly payment stays at £1,359.76, even if interest rates change.

scenes.title: When your fixed rate ends
scenes.narration: Your fixed rate ends on 31 October 2028. After that, you move to our Standard Variable Rate. It's 7.49 percent today, and it can go up or down. If it stays the same, your payment would rise to £1,770.43 a month. That's £410.67 more. Many people choose a new deal before their fixed rate ends.

scenes.title: Paying off early

visual.footnote: Overpay up to 10% a year with no charge.

scenes.narration: You can pay off up to 10 percent of what you owe each year at no extra cost. If you repay more than that during your fixed rate, there's an early repayment charge. It's 2 percent in year 1 and 1 percent in year 2. For example, repaying an extra ten thousand pounds in year 1 would cost £200.

scenes.narration: Over the full 30 years, you'd repay about £627,498 in total, if rates don't change. That includes your loan of £256,500 and the interest on it.
